meta.titre: Cameroon Constitution and State Institutions: the arms of government and their work
meta.sous_theme: The 1996 Constitution, separation of powers and the duties of office holders

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A school has a set of regulations that bind pupils, teachers and the principal alike. Nobody may make a school rule that breaks the regulations. A country works in the same way: no law, no order and no action by an official may go against the Constitution. At the GCE you are asked in which year the Constitution was adopted, what it changed, which institutions it sets up and what their members must do. A clear picture of the three arms of government gives you the answer to many of these questions.

items: A law is a rule made by an authority that everyone must obey.
Citizens vote to choose some of their leaders.
Cameroon has two official languages, English and French.

sections.titre: The Constitution and the institutions of the State
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What a constitution is
A **constitution** is the supreme law of a country. It sets up the institutions of the State, defines their powers, protects the rights of citizens and limits the power of those who govern.

### The Cameroon Constitution
The present Constitution dates from **1996**. It revised the earlier Constitution of 1972. It declares Cameroon a decentralised unitary State that is one and indivisible, secular, democratic and social, and it gives English and French equal status as official languages.

### Some innovations of 1996
- A second chamber of Parliament, the **Senate**.
- Decentralisation, with **Regions** as local authorities.
- A **Constitutional Council** to check that laws respect the Constitution.

Some of these provisions were put into practice only years later. The Senate began to work in 2013 and the Constitutional Council was installed in 2018.

### The three arms of government (separation of powers)
| Arm | Institutions | Main work |
|---|---|---|
| Executive | President of the Republic, Prime Minister, ministers | Runs the country and carries out the laws |
| Legislative | Parliament: the National Assembly and the Senate | Makes laws, votes the budget, controls the Government |
| Judicial | Courts and tribunals | Interpret the law, settle disputes, punish offences |

The **Constitutional Council** checks that laws conform to the Constitution and handles disputes about certain elections.

### Responsibilities of a member of Parliament
A deputy or a senator represents the people, takes part in making laws and in voting the budget, questions the Government on its action, and speaks for the needs of the people he or she represents.

### Fighting corruption
The Constitution requires some senior office holders to declare their assets when they take up and when they leave office. The National Anti-Corruption Commission also works to prevent and fight corruption.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to name or explain the arms of government
variantes.contenu_markdown: Learn one verb for each: the legislative makes laws, the executive applies them, the judiciary interprets and enforces them. Always add the institutions, such as Parliament for the legislative and the courts for the judiciary.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the year, or for innovations, or for provisions put into practice later
variantes.contenu_markdown: The year is 1996. For innovations give two items among the Senate, decentralised Regions and the Constitutional Council. For provisions applied later, the Senate and the Constitutional Council are good choices because they were set up years after the text was adopted.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the responsibility of a member of Parliament or of another officer
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the duty with a short reason: represent the people of the constituency so that their needs are heard, vote laws so that rules are made for society, question ministers so that the Government is controlled.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the separation of powers helps to prevent the abuse of power in Cameroon. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and state the idea.
etapes.justification: Explain needs reasons. The key idea is that power is shared among different institutions.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Separation of powers means that the legislative, executive and judicial powers are held by different institutions.

etapes.action: Give the three arms with their work.
etapes.justification: The examiner expects the arms to be named before they are linked to the idea of abuse.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Parliament makes laws, the executive runs the country and the courts interpret the law.

etapes.action: Link each arm to the control of the others.
etapes.justification: This is the reasoning that earns the marks, because it shows the mechanism.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Parliament questions the Government and votes the budget, so the executive cannot spend without approval. The courts can punish illegal acts, so nobody is above the law. The executive carries out the laws, so Parliament's decisions are applied.

etapes.action: Add the role of the Constitution and close.
etapes.justification: The Constitution is what fixes the powers of each arm.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Constitution defines the powers of each institution. No arm may go beyond them.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: Separation of powers means that the power to make laws, to carry them out and to judge is given to different institutions. In Cameroon, Parliament makes laws, the President, the Prime Minister and the ministers run the country, and the courts interpret the law. This helps to prevent abuse. Parliament votes the budget and questions the Government, so the executive cannot spend or act without control. The courts judge cases, so officials who break the law can be punished. The executive applies the laws that Parliament has voted. Finally the Constitution sets the limits of each institution, so no single person or group can take all the power.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Senate is made up of ministers."
items.pourquoi_faux: The Senate is one of the two chambers of Parliament and its members are senators. Ministers belong to the executive.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate.

items.pourquoi_faux: Laws are voted by Parliament. The courts interpret the law and apply it to cases.
items.correction_markdown: Make laws: Parliament. Apply and interpret: the courts.

items.erreur_markdown: "The present Constitution of Cameroon was adopted in 1972."
items.pourquoi_faux: 1972 is the year of the earlier Constitution. The present Constitution dates from 1996.
items.correction_markdown: Give 1996 and say that it revised the Constitution of 1972.

items.erreur_markdown: "A constitution exists to protect those in power."
items.pourquoi_faux: A constitution limits the power of the rulers and protects the rights of citizens.
items.correction_markdown: Say that it sets up institutions, limits their powers and protects rights.

items.erreur_markdown: "A deputy is an administrative officer who keeps order in the constituency."
items.pourquoi_faux: Keeping order in a unit is the work of administrative officers such as the Divisional Officer. A deputy is an elected representative of the people.
items.correction_markdown: State the duty: represent the people, make laws, vote the budget and control the Government.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Name the three arms of government. (b) State one function of each.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The legislature, the executive and the judiciary. (b) The legislature makes laws; the executive runs the country and carries out the laws; the judiciary interprets the law and settles disputes. Award one mark for each arm and one for each function.

items.enonce_markdown: Describe three responsibilities of a member of Parliament towards the people he or she represents.
items.solution_markdown: Any three, each with a short reason: represent the people so that their problems are heard; take part in making and voting laws that affect their lives; vote the budget and watch how public money is used; question the Government so that it explains its action; keep contact with the people to know their needs. Award one mark for the responsibility and one for the explanation of each.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Explain two innovations of the 1996 Constitution. (b) Why can some provisions of a constitution take many years to be applied?
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any two: the Senate was created as a second chamber of Parliament, which gives a second look at laws; the Regions were created as decentralised local authorities, which gives local people a bigger part in managing their affairs; the Constitutional Council checks that laws conform to the Constitution. (b) A provision often needs further laws and decrees to explain how it will work, institutions must be built and staffed, money must be provided, and elections or appointments must be organised. All of this takes time. Award marks for each innovation with an explanation and for two reasons in (b).

items_markdown: A constitution is the supreme law: it sets up institutions, limits power and protects rights.
The present Constitution of Cameroon dates from 1996 and revised the 1972 Constitution.
Innovations include the Senate, decentralised Regions and the Constitutional Council. The Senate and the Council began to work years later.
The legislature makes laws, the executive applies them and the judiciary interprets them. Sharing power prevents abuse.
A member of Parliament represents the people, takes part in making laws and controls the Government.
